It treats the volume as a translucent gel or gas, simulating light absorption and emission as rays pass through the scalar field [S17, unofficial][S16][S4, unofficial].

The claim states that the technique treats the volume as a translucent gel or gas, simulating light absorption and emission as rays pass through the scalar field. Source [S17] explicitly states that in direct volume rendering, 'The optical attributes like a color, an opacity, or an emission are assigned directly to the voxels' and that 'scalar value given at a sample point is virtually mapped to physical quantities that describe the emission and absorption of light'. It further confirms that 'rays are cast... and perform the process of resampling the volume'. Source [S16] corroborates this by describing the simulation of 'light absorption along rays cast through the voxel data' and the accumulation of 'colour and opacity values'. Source [S4] describes DVR as displaying 'transparent volume areas' by shooting rays through the volumetric dataset. The metaphor 'translucent gel or gas' aligns with the description of treating the volume as a continuous medium with optical properties (opacity/absorption) rather than discrete surfaces, which is the core definition of Direct Volume Rendering provided in the sources.
